newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine eyes higher oil refining throughput in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine eyes higher oil refining throughput in 1997.

text.p: Ukraine has forecast oil refining throughput to rise to 22.0 million tonnes in 1997 (about 440,000 barrels per day, or bpd), from 13.4 million tonnes in 1996 (268,000 bpd), a senior energy official said on Monday.
"Our plans envision 22 million tonnes of oil refined this year," Stepan Yaloveha, spokesman for the State Oil and Gas Committee, told Reuters.
He said the government would import 18 million tonnes of crude oil in 1997 and that the balance would come from domestic reserves.
"We have plans to widen our oil import sources and buy oil not only from Russia, but from Kazakhstan, from Azerbajan and maybe from Gulf countries," he said.
Officials had targeted oil imports in 1996 at 12.3 million tonnes, but the actual total was about nine million tonnes.
The Statistics Ministry reported on Monday that total domestic oil output slipped last year to 3.7 million tonnes from 4.0 million tonnes in 1995.
It said Ukraine produced 2.8 million tonnes of gasoline in 1996 compared to 2.9 million tonnes in 1995.
It produced 3.8 million tonnes of heavy fuel oil, or mazut, against 4.3 million tonnes in 1995.
Both figures reflected lower Russian crude oil supplies.
Ukraine's six refineries processed up to 60 million tonnes (1.2 million bpd) of crude oil a year in Soviet times, but are now working far below capacity.
